quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO Susan Li): family of apps revenue was $58.9 billion, up 25% year over year; family of apps ad revenue was $58.1 billion, up 24% (23% on a constant currency basis). Ad impressions increased 18% (driven primarily by engagement and user growth) and the average price per ad increased 6%, 'benefiting from increased advertiser demand largely driven by improved ad performance'. Family of apps other revenue was $801 million, up 54%, on WhatsApp paid revenue growth and MetaVerified subscriptions. Reality Labs revenue was $955 million, down 12% (lapping the Quest 3s introduction). More than 3.5 billion people used at least one app daily in December; employees ended Q4 at over 78,800, up 6%, driven by hiring in priority areas (the transcript names infrastructure and Meta Superintelligence before the text breaks off). Online commerce was the largest contributor to year-over-year ad growth, followed by professional services and technology.
quarterly_data.figure: family of apps revenue $58.9 billion (up 25%); family of apps ad revenue $58.1 billion (up 24%); ad impressions increased 18%; average price per ad increased 6%; Reality Labs revenue $955 million (down 12%)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (CFO): Q1 2026 total revenue expected in the range of $53.5 billion to $56.5 billion, assuming foreign currency is an approximately 4% tailwind to year-over-year growth ('a three-point larger tailwind than it was in Q4 2025'); the range 'embeds an outlook for accelerated growth', underpinned by strong demand through the end of Q4 and into the start of 2026. Full-year 2026 total expenses expected at $162 to $169 billion; 'The majority of expense growth will be driven by infrastructure costs, which includes third-party cloud spend, higher depreciation, and higher infrastructure operating expenses', with compensation for technical talent (particularly AI) the second-largest contributor; Reality Labs operating losses expected similar to 2025. 'Despite the meaningful step-up in infrastructure investment, in 2026, we expect to deliver operating income that is above 2025 operating income' (absolute dollars, not growth). 2026 tax rate expected at 13% to 16%. Later in the year growth may be tempered by fading currency tailwinds, lapping stronger 2025 periods and the revised less personalized ads offering in the EU. (The call also gave the 2026 capex range already recorded from the Meta 10-K entry.)
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue $53.5 billion to $56.5 billion; FY2026 total expenses $162 to $169 billion; 2026 tax rate 13% to 16%

quarterly_data.signal: MetaCompute (CEO Mark Zuckerberg): Meta 'will continue to invest very significantly in infrastructure to train leading models and deliver personal superintelligence to billions of people and businesses around the world'. MetaCompute was announced 'with the belief that being the most efficient at how we engineer, invest, and partner to build our infrastructure will become a strategic advantage'. Dina Powell McCormick joined as president and vice chairman to lead partnering with governments, sovereigns and strategic capital partners to expand long-term capacity. 'An important part of MetaCompute will be making long-term investments in silicon and energy. We will continue working with key partners while advancing our own silicon program. We're architecting our systems so that we can be flexible in the systems that we use, and we expect the cost per gigawatt to decrease significantly over time through optimizing both our technology and supply chain.'

Compute supply (CFO, asked about internal compute needs): 'we do continue to be capacity constrained.' Teams ramped up infrastructure and are improving infrastructure efficiency by 'optimizing workloads, improving infrastructure utilization, diversifying our chip supply, and just investing in efficiency improvements'. On ads, 'we think that there is room for our larger models to benefit from having more compute', and scaling the compute available to the foundational ranking and recommendation models is expected to bring gains. Q4 infrastructure expense growth was driven by higher depreciation, cloud spend and other operating expenses.

Ads-model compute scaling (CFO): in Q4 GEM was extended to Facebook reels and now covers all major surfaces across Facebook and Instagram; 'We also doubled the size of the GPU cluster we used to train it. In 2026, we're expecting to meaningfully scale up GEM training to an even larger cluster', increasing model complexity and training data and using a new sequence learning architecture begun in Q4. 'This is the first time we have found a recommendation model architecture that can scale with similar efficiency as LLMs.' A new runtime ads-inference model across Instagram feed, stories and reels drove a 3% increase in conversion rates in Q4; consolidating Facebook models under Lattice plus back-end improvements drove a 12% increase in ad quality, and in 2026 Meta expects to consolidate more models than in the prior two years. Meta is also building new recommendation model architectures that work on top of LLMs.
quarterly_data.figure: GEM training GPU cluster doubled in Q4; 3% increase in conversion rates; 12% increase in ad quality

quarterly_data.signal: Infrastructure build and financing (CFO): to keep long-term flexibility Meta is 'changing how we develop data center sites, establishing strategic partnerships, contracting cloud capacity, and establishing new ownership structures for some of our large data center sites.' Cash generation is expected to fund 2026 infrastructure investments, but Meta will 'periodically supplement our strong operating cash flow with prudent amounts of cost-efficient external financing, which may lead us to eventually maintain a positive net debt balance.' No additional data-center/compute JV to announce; Meta is weighing different paths to stand up capacity against 'a very wide range of possible capacity demand over the years to come'. Q4 (the transcript text is garbled here and the line-item name is cut off): '... were $22.1 billion, driven by investments in data centers, servers, and network infrastructure'; free cash flow was $14.1 billion; quarter-end cash and marketable securities $81.6 billion and debt $58.7 billion. The 2026 capex growth is 'driven by increased investment to support our Meta Superintelligence Labs efforts and core business'.
quarterly_data.figure: $22.1 billion (Q4, data centers, servers and network infrastructure); free cash flow $14.1 billion; cash and marketable securities $81.6 billion; debt $58.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Models and AI products (CEO/CFO): 'In '25, we rebuilt the foundations of our AI program'; Meta Superintelligence Labs is about six months in, new models and products will ship 'over the coming months', and Meta expects to 'steadily push the frontier over the course of the year'. Meta is working on merging LLMs with the recommendation systems behind Facebook, Instagram, Threads and ads. Meta AI is available in over 200 markets; AI dubbing supports nine languages with hundreds of millions of people watching AI-translated videos every day; nearly 10% of reels viewed each day are created in the Edits app; Meta AI daily actives generating media tripled year over year. The Manus acquisition will be integrated into ads and business manager. Glasses sales 'more than tripled last year'; Reality Labs investment is shifting mostly to glasses and wearables, with 2026 losses similar to last year and likely the peak.
quarterly_data.figure: Meta AI available in over 200 markets; nearly 10% of reels created in Edits; glasses sales more than tripled

quarterly_data.signal: Business AI and internal AI adoption (CFO): paid messaging within WhatsApp crossed a $2 billion annual run rate in Q4; click-to-message ads revenue growth accelerated with the US up more than 50% year over year; over 1 million weekly conversations between people and business AIs (early traction in Mexico and the Philippines), expanding to more markets in 2026; the Meta AI business assistant is in testing with advertisers. Internally, 'Since the beginning of 2025, we've seen a 30% increase in output per engineer', mostly from agentic coding adoption (a big jump in Q4); output of power users of AI coding tools increased 80% year over year.
